Whose war is it anyway

By: Johann Botha | Production

Proposal


Show:

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
On Monday a huge arms cache was discovered in Randburg.

Summary:
Amnesty for illegal guns have never yielded the required result. Very few if any of the weapons handed in have been successfully linked to crimes. Yet illegal firearms including automatic assault weapons, explosives and live ammunition is quite easy to buy, if you know where to shop. The cache found by construction workers on Monday in Randburg, once again underlines how vulnerable we are to attacks of terror. These finds are usually made by accident because it is so easy to hide, and almost impossible for the police to find. Does the fact that we haven't had a large attack similar to other world cities mean that we are safer, or does it mean that we are sitting on a time bomb and that the fuse is getting ever shorter with every "attack free" day we have in our country?

Further information:
Wynand: comment: no buying guns. cant do this legally.

Press Release:


Terror Arms Cache
A large cache of assault weapons including bombs, hand grenades, a suicide vest and automatic rifles were found in a building in Randburg. Experts believe it’s an unusual
choice of weapons for Johannesburg’s criminal underworld, so could these arms be intended for terror attacks on our shores? Carte Blanche investigates whether South
Africa’s defence and intelligence systems are prepared to face possible terrorist threats.

Script:


17/09/11





Graphic
9/11/2001 will be remembered as the day the world changed forever. A month later, the US invaded Afghanistan and two years later also Iraq. Extremist muslim groupings started striking back with more terror attacks in the cities and countries of their opponents. Na'eem Jeenah of the Afro Middle-East Centre watches these events closely

Na'eem
What is called now Islamic State, previously Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant, and previously Islamic State of Iraq, previously Al-Queda of the Land of the Two Rivers.... all came out of the American occupation.

During the entire 1970's only 244 people were killed globally in attacks for which muslim terror groups claimed responsibility.
In the 1980's this figure rose to 657.
During the turbulent 1990's, there were 1049 related mortalities.
Then 9/11 happened, and over the next ten years, the deaths increased 8-fold.

Now, only 6 years into the next decade, the death toll has overtaken the extreme figure of the previous decade.. Many of these attacks take place in the war-torn areas themselves, but there have been numerous attacks on big cities elsewhere – Paris, London, and most recently in S Petersburg in Russia.
Last week an arms cache was found in the heart of Randburg in Gauteng
Devi link
Extremist or terror attacks have become a part daily global life. But thankfully here at the tip of Africa, that does not seem to be one of our more pressing problems. Or, has that changed?

Construction workers discovered a suspicious bag in this building, literally 300m from the very busy Randburg taxi ranks. The police then found a bigger cache in the basement. Only a few visual images were released, together with a list showing a large array of arms including different assault rifles, 60 mortars, hand grenades, 10 kg's of plastic explosives and a suicide bomber’s vest. The vest is by far the most worrying item on their list, as this is the first one to be found in South Africa. But, the vest was not shown in the police photos, making experts like Na'eem skeptical, because last year in the case of the Thulsie twins, the police wrongly claimed that they possessed a suicide vest.
Na'eem
The Hawks put out these pictures of the suicide vest that was found in their house, it turns out that it was a vest that is used for their paintball adventures rather than for blowing up things.

Na'eem does not feel that South Africa is a target for extremist muslim groups
Na'eem
I don't think that any of them see South Africa as a useful target. Why, because certainly the kind of value of blowing up something in South Africa is not as great as blowing up something in Europe.

Jasmin Opperman from terror watch-dog Trac disagrees
Jasmine
Irrespective if it's Johannesburg or London, an attack is an attack. It will have propaganda value. It will lead to a claim of success. It will propagate a message of we are omnipresent, we can do and execute anytime we want. And that is the foundation we need to understand.

Jasmine says she traced and interviewed 12 members of the Islamic State and Al Keida who are based in South Africa
jasmine
In response to questions related “Will you execute an attack?There was a general response. If being instructed, yes, we will. Because that will be God's calling

The photos of the cache show that the arms differ vastly in age and in condition. Lobo das Neves is one of Africa's top weapons experts
Lobo
These appear to be Mills’ Grenades from the second world war. You see firearms in 2 conditions. Some of the firearms appear to be ready for use immediately, and some of those firearms seem to have been decayed through rust

Some of them are local and could only have originated from our own police or armed forces
Lobo
R5 is a South African manufactured full automatic assault rifle only, mainly issued to the South African Police Service

These hand grenades, filled with deadly shrapnel, are also South African made
Lobo
In fact no member of the police, unless that policeman is specially trained and assigned to a special unit, may be in possession of one of those.

Plastic explosives can also cause tremendous damage
Lobo
With 10kg's of plastic explosives, you can sink a war ship

Lobo says it is unlikely to be a terrorist cache
Lobo
A trained terrorist would make sure that his arms cache is firstly in a place where the arms won't be discovered and secondly in a place where they are safe in other words where wheather and other elements won't damage the weapons, because when you need them they have to be servicable.

He feels that organised crime cannot be ruled out as the purpose of the cache – it is not rare to see assault rifles being used in robberies. Recently we've also seen a dramatic increase in the use of explosives, not just in ATM bombings, but also in other robberies and, as we saw last week, even in cash in transit heists.
Lobo
We look at ATM bombing, bank robberies have happened where people get threatened with explosives, hand grenades. So explosives form a part of the crime in this country.

The proximity of the cache to the Randburg taxi ranks and many cross border destinations could also indicate that the weapons were in transit
Jasmine
Weapons smuggling into Mozambique and Renamo is a reality being used by former Renamo soldiers, now fighters, that's involved in organised crime in Mozambique. So the question of how the weapons would have been used must be seen in a regional context and not only a local context.

Another expert theory links the cache to fighting pirates. A few years ago a number of new South African maritime security companies started up, to offer protection to commercial ships heading up on the East Coast of Africa. Because of our anti-mercenary legislation, they battled to get firearm licenses, and, we were told, some then acquired them illegally on the black market. The sources (who did not want to be identified), believe this cache is a remnant from one of those ventures, which now ended up in Johannesburg, looking for new buyers.
Peter Jacobs is a maritime security expert, and he strongly disputes this theory
Peter
I don't think it is true. The maritime environment is quite heavily regulated. So, I find that sort of situation very very difficult to believe.

Which brings us back to the terror theory. Two of the weapons found in the cache are seldom seen in southern Africa, but are common to the north, where extremist groupings have their strongholds. One is an AK74, for some reason not identified by the police on their list, and the other a fully automatic M16.
MAYBE DROP THIS Lobo
M16 is an American-made assault rifle that also comes in a full automatic and semi automatic variety. Those are also fairly rare and expensive in South Africa.

And then there is still the question of the suicide vest...Reliable sources inside the police and crime intelligence told us that the suicide vest is the real deal – and even more worrying - that it was packed with explosives, steel ballbearings, and was ready to detonate. Despite various attempts, we could not officially substantiate these claims. The police cite the sensitivity of the investigation as their reason for declining an interview or any further comments.
Jasmine
Suicide vests are not being used in organised crime activities. Suicide vests are not being used in Mozambique because it's so closely linked to organised crime. Why on home soil? Yes, it could be merely on transit somewhere else. But it narrows it down to a possible activity of extremism that will have to be properly investigated.

It is certainly worrying that the cache was stumbled upon accidentally, but at the same time, the fact that the construction workers reported it immediately is commendable.
Lobo
It is common knowledge that in Tel Aviv, Jerusalem, an unattended package remains unattended for approximately 60 seconds before it's reported. 60 Seconds! People are attuned to it by now to see someone putting down the backpack and report it and maybe even arresting the person.

Even if this cache is not linked to extremists – the fact remains that we live in an increasingly radicalised society and that weapons of warfare are far too readily available to criminals or even to so-called lone wolves who see it as their calling to save the world from some perceived evil – and this is the real terror of the world we live in today
Lone wolf statement
One person wakes up, decides to do this and does it. That's always possible. Whether you're talking about someone that's inspired by the Islamic State Group or someone that's inspired by the Boeremag. That's Possible.




Link 15 secs
Was the arms cache found in Randburg last week linked to terror, fighting piracy or organised crime
But it narrows it down to possible extremist activities


Link 15 secs
How seriously should we be concerned about the arms cache found in Randburg last week?

With 10kg's of explosives, you can sink a war ship

And what about the suicide bombers vest police claime they also found
